description: Poll a Cohesity cluster REST API for storage and protection metrics
documentation: One endpoint is one Cohesity cluster. Authentication is a cluster API key, sent as the apiKey header - not a username and password, whose session token expires after 24 hours and would have to be refreshed. Generate the key in the Cohesity UI under Settings > Access Management > API Keys. The key can either be pasted into this configuration or held in the Dynatrace credential vault and selected here; exactly one of the two, and the extension refuses a configuration that sets both or neither.

name.description: Friendly name used in extension logs. Metric dimensions carry the cluster's own id and name, read from the API, so renaming this does not orphan anything.

host.description: Hostname, VIP or IP address of the Cohesity cluster. The ActiveGate must be able to reach it.

useCredentialVault.description: Read the Cohesity API key from a stored Dynatrace credential instead of pasting it here. The ActiveGate resolves the vault entry and injects its value before the extension runs, so the key is never held in this monitoring configuration. Recommended when the same key is shared by more than one configuration, or when key rotation is owned by somebody other than whoever edits this page.

credentialVaultId.description: The stored credential holding the Cohesity cluster API key. Create it under Settings > Credential vault as a token credential, and make sure its access scope lets this ActiveGate group read it - a credential the ActiveGate cannot read resolves to nothing, and the extension reports that as a vault problem rather than as a bad key.

apiKey.description: Sent as the apiKey header on every request. Accepted as-is: the extension only refuses an empty value or one containing whitespace, because the key format is not guaranteed to be the same across Cohesity 6.8 to 7.4 and rejecting a valid key is worse than surfacing a bad one as an authentication error.

verifyTls.description: Leave on. Cohesity ships a self-signed certificate, so either trust its CA on the ActiveGate and point at it below, or accept that turning this off exposes the API key to anything that can answer for the cluster address.

caCertPath.description: Absolute path on the ActiveGate, readable by the ActiveGate service user. Leave empty to use the system trust store.

fixtureDir.description: Leave empty for normal operation. When set, the extension reads every response from recorded JSON in this directory on the ActiveGate and makes no network calls at all - it is how the extension is demonstrated and debugged without a cluster. The responses shipped with the extension are SYNTHETIC: hand-written from Cohesity's published schemas, not captured from a cluster. Every poll logs a warning saying so.

collectStorageDomains.description: Per storage domain (view box) capacity and consumption. This is the only switch: the matching extension feature set mirrors it rather than gating separately, so turning this off stops both the API calls and the ingest.

collectViews.description: Read and write throughput for the top 20 views by activity, carried as dimensions on a cluster metric - views are not entities, because a top-N ranking makes an unstable entity population. Turning this off skips the API calls, not just the ingest.

collectProtection.description: Protection groups, their runs and SLA outcomes. This is the most expensive feature set on a large estate - one call per group per interval.

collectHostLink.displayName: Link protection groups to Dynatrace hosts (VMware only)
collectHostLink.description: Off by default, and the only collection that is. When on, the extension asks a few VMware protection groups per poll for the BIOS UUID of each VM they back up, and emits one metric line per VM so a workflow can draw a 'protects' edge from the protection group to the Dynatrace HOST. That is ONE SERIES PER PROTECTED VM - a bounded-scale mechanism, not a general one - so it is capped by 'Protected objects per poll' below and restricted to VMware groups, which are the only ones that publish a UUID at all. It also does nothing on its own: the OpenPipeline routing entry and the sync workflow have to be installed once. See the extension README.

maxHostLinkObjects.displayName: Protected objects per poll (host link cap)
maxHostLinkObjects.description: The hard ceiling on how many protected VMs one poll may publish as metric lines, and therefore on the cardinality this feature can add. When the cap truncates, the extension says so as a WARN on its diagnostics log channel - the mapping published is then PARTIAL and hosts beyond the cap get no edge, which would otherwise look exactly like part of the estate going unprotected. Raise it only if the resulting series count is acceptable on this tenant.

intervalMinutes.description: Cluster capacity moves slowly. Polling faster than the cluster's own stats refresh only costs API calls.

maxRunFanoutGroups.displayName: Run fan-out budget (protection groups per poll)
maxRunFanoutGroups.description: Only used when the cluster-wide runs endpoints are unavailable and runs have to be read one protection group at a time. This is how many requests one poll may spend on that, not a limit on how many groups are monitored: the fan-out continues from where the previous poll stopped, so every group is reached within (groups / this) polls. Lower it on a cluster that is struggling to answer; raise it to see every group sooner.

collectAlerts.description: Off by default. When on, the extension sends the cluster's own health alerts - node, disk, capacity and similar - to Dynatrace as log records under the source cohesity_storage.alerts, de-duplicated so a still-open alert is not re-sent every poll. These describe the CLUSTER, not the data it protects: no usernames, no source addresses and no backup content. The one field that can name something in the protected estate is the free-form description, which has its own switch below.

alertDescriptions.description: On by default, and only consulted when alerts are collected. The description is the sentence that says what actually broke, and it is also the only alert field that can contain a name from the protected estate - a datastore, a share, occasionally a VM. Turn it off to keep the alert and drop the sentence: id, name, severity, category, state and timestamps are all still sent.

alertLookbackHours.description: How far back each poll asks for alerts. Wider than the poll interval on purpose, so an alert raised just after a poll is not missed; the de-duplication ledger, not this window, is what stops an alert being sent twice. Raise it after an outage to backfill.

maxAlerts.description: A ceiling on how many alerts one poll will read. A cluster in a bad state can raise a great many at once, and this bounds what that costs in ingest.

alertSeverityFloor.description: The least severe alert worth sending, applied as a REQUEST filter so that less severe alerts do not consume the per-poll budget below. That matters: on the cluster this was built against, a 24h window holds more alerts than one poll may read, so info-level alerts were crowding out critical ones after every restart. If the cluster ignores the filter the extension still drops them locally and says so on the diagnostics channel - the budget is just not recovered.
The least severe alert worth sending.
